body.statement:
Assume \(L_\pi\ge1/2\).  Let \(\widetilde C_n\) be any replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private interval satisfying
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in\widetilde C_n\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
If \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), then
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(\widetilde C_n)]
 \ge c\left[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \vee\left\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\right\}\right].
\]
The constant \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).  The lower bound uses a randomized-treatment, uniform-design, strictly positive regression submodel and contains no \(q<\gamma\) paired-cell branch.
body.justification: This theorem separates the sound full-class privacy limitation from the stronger attainable-submodel upper result.
body.gap: Existing private pointwise regression bounds concern noncausal regression experiments; the theorem embeds that barrier into honest causal intervals on the unchanged positive-density class.
body.consumer: Reviewers and privacy-budget committees obtain a defensible lower benchmark without relying on the rejected paired-microcell transport argument.
body.proof_tex:
Choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(\varphi\), supported on \([-1,1]^d\), with \(\varphi(0)=1\).  Put
\(p_* = \min\{1/4,L_\mu/2\}>0\).  Choose a constant \(a_*>0\), depending only on \((L_\tau,p_*,\gamma,d)\), so small that for every \(0<h\le r_0\),
\[
 g_h(x)=a_*h^\gamma\varphi((x-x_0)/h)
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal H^\gamma(L_\tau;\mathcal X)\) and obeys \(0\le g_h\le p_*/2\).  This is possible because each derivative of order \(j\le\lfloor\gamma\rfloor\) scales as \(a_*h^{\gamma-j}\), while the top-order H\"older seminorm is bounded by a constant times \(a_*\).  The support lies in \(\mathcal X\) by the boundary and bandwidth conditions.

Define two full-data laws \(Q_0,Q_h\) as follows.  Under both, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal X\), \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and \(A\) is conditionally independent of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X\).  Under \(Q_0\), conditional on \(X\), take \(Y(0),Y(1)\) independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(p_*\).  Under \(Q_h\), use respective means \(p_*\) and \(p_*+g_h(X)\).  In both laws set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  These laws have common support \(\{0,1\}\), satisfy consistency and ignorability by construction, satisfy overlap because \(\kappa<1/2\), and satisfy both density bounds because \(\underline f\le1\le\overline f\).  The constant propensity belongs to its H\"older ball by \(L_\pi\ge1/2\); the constant control regression belongs to its ball by the choice of \(p_*\); and the CATEs are \(0\) and \(g_h\).  Hence \(Q_0,Q_h\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Their causal target separation is
\[
 \Delta_h=|\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)-\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)|=a_*h^\gamma.
\]

Let \(P_0,P_h\) be the corresponding one-record observed laws.  A direct calculation in the treated Bernoulli stratum gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_h\|P_0)
 =\frac12\int_{\mathcal X}\frac{g_h(x)^2}{p_*(1-p_*)}\,dx
 \le C_\chi h^{2\gamma+d},
\]
and
\[
 \|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int_{\mathcal X}g_h(x)\,dx
 \le C_v h^{\gamma+d}.
\]
Both constants are fixed and finite because \(p_*\in(0,1/2)\) and \(\varphi\) is bounded with compact support.

For the privacy-free part, likelihood factorization and Fubini give the exact product identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(P_h^n\|P_0^n)=\{1+\chi^2(P_h\|P_0)\}^n.
\]
Also, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the product likelihood ratio \(L\) gives
\[
 \|P_h^n-P_0^n\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\mathbb E_{P_0^n}|L-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_h^n\|P_0^n)}.
\]
Taking \(h=c_1n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\), with \(c_1\le r_0\) sufficiently small, makes the last total variation at most \(1/8\).  Passing the sample through any randomized interval mechanism cannot increase total variation, since for every output event the difference is an integral of a function taking values in \([0,1]\).

For the privacy part, take
\[
 h=c_2\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}^{1/(\gamma+d)},
\]
where \(c_2\le r_0\) is chosen so that
\(\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le a_0\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}\) and
\(a_0(e-1+c_0)\le1/8\).  The Hamming-transport lemma, \(e^u-1\le(e-1)u\) for \(0\le u\le1\), and \(n\delta_n\le c_0\) imply
\[
 \|P_h^n\mathsf K-P_0^n\mathsf K\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le n\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
       (e^{\epsilon_n}-1+\delta_n)
 \le a_0(e-1+c_0)\le\frac18,
\]
where \(\mathsf K\) denotes the interval-release kernel.

It remains to turn either indistinguishable pair into a length bound.  Let \(\nu_j\) denote the two output laws, let \(\theta_j\) be their target values, and set \(E_j=\{\theta_j\in\widetilde C_n\}\).  Honesty gives \(\nu_j(E_j)\ge1-\eta\).  If \(\|\nu_0-\nu_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1/8\), then
\[
 \nu_0(E_0\cap E_1)
 \ge \nu_0(E_0)+\nu_0(E_1)-1
 \ge 1-2\eta-\frac18>\frac38.
\]
On this intersection the interval has length at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|=\Delta_h\).  Therefore its expected length under \(Q_0\) is at least \(3\Delta_h/8\).  The first bandwidth gives the term \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), and the second gives
\(1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\).  Applying the two conclusions separately to the same arbitrary mechanism and taking the smaller of their fixed constants proves the maximum of the two terms.

The truncation by one is necessary: the deterministic interval \([-1,1]\) is private, honest, and has length two, so the untruncated expression in the frozen statement cannot hold uniformly as \(n\epsilon_n\downarrow0\).
